subject: Mutual Action Plan: hosting mode & regional runway for Cardio.IO
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen@cardio.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cardio.IO Procurement <procurement@cardio.io>
Date: 2026-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — hosting mode + region constraints

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's latency profile. We want to lock the deployment path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and the regional footprint as part of the MAP so procurement can schedule budget and security can finalize the checklist. Key constraints: PHI-in-scope (US), preferred primary region: us-west, backup: us-east, timeline: production by end of Q3 if feasible.

Can you propose a MAP with evaluation milestones and a recommended canary strategy for us? We've attached our draft requirements (security_requirements_2026.pdf) and a blank MAP sheet.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Sr. Eng Manager, Cardio.IO

Attachments: security_requirements_2026.pdf (PDF, 412KB), Cardio_IO_MAP_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen@cardio.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting mode + region constraints

Hi Helen — great to hear the demo resonated. I've sketched an initial MAP and a short eval plan for the hosting/region decision and attached it. High level recommendation up front: run a quick 2-week functional PoC on Hosted (us-west) to validate integrations and latency, then a 3-week scale test on Dedicated (same region) to measure tail latency and cost at target QPS. Private (on-prem/VPC) remains available for late-stage regulated scope if audit evidence requires it; we should keep legal/procurement engaged early.

Proposed MAP milestones (brief):
- Week 0: Formalize MAP & success criteria (latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, data residency)
- Weeks 1-2: Hosted PoC (dev traffic, integration smoke tests, KV cache validation)
- Weeks 3-5: Dedicated scale test (load, failover, autoscale policy)
- Week 6: Security / compliance evidence review and decision checkpoint (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Procurement: parallel cadence — contract redlines and SOW by Week 6-8

I'll bold a few decisions for the canary: start with Hosted for non-sensitive traffic and run a 5% canary of real user requests once integration is green, then shift to Dedicated if we need predictable throughput for production. If Cardio.IO needs full data isolation or HSM-backed KMS, we recommend Private and can present a migration runway.

Attaching: Cardio_IO_MAP_v1_populated.xlsx (MAP + milestones) and a short ops checklist. Can you confirm: (1) target QPS for production, (2) any corporate firewall/VPN constraints for Dedicated, (3) procurement SLAs for contract turnaround?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Cardio_IO_MAP_v1_populated.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Helen Park <helen@cardio.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting mode + region constraints

One more datapoint from pricing/ops perspective. If Cardio.IO expects steady-state QPS > 150 req/s at 8k token windows, Dedicated becomes materially cheaper at scale given reserved capacity discounts and predictable batching. A quick cost sensitivity check we can run during the Dedicated scale test: compare per-token unit economics (Hosted burst vs Dedicated reserved) at 150/300/600 QPS.

Notes for the MAP doc: please add an "economics" column with threshold QPS where Dedicated pays off and a runbook row for fallback to Hosted in cross-region outage. I'll prepare a short model and drop it into the shared Drive link.

-Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen@cardio.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting mode + region constraints

Helen — quick security note from our side. The PDF you sent clarified PHI scope, which pushes a few mandatory checks for Hosted: (1) retention controls with customer-configured TTLs, (2) audit logs export to your SIEM (we can enable a dedicated forwarder for us-west), and (3) KMS integration — Hosted supports envelope encryption; if you require HSM-backed keys under your control we need Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.

If you can confirm which data classes are allowed to flow to Hosted during the PoC (e.g., pseudonymized tokens only), we can tailor the PoC and the canary gating rules. Otherwise we’ll assume non-PHI for Hosted canary traffic.

-Laura
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Helen Park <helen@cardio.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cardio.IO Procurement <procurement@cardio.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-25T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting mode + region constraints

Thanks, team — the MAP looks good and procurement has penciled in budget contingent on passing the Dedicated scale test. Confirming answers:
1) Target steady-state: 200 QPS avg at 4k token windows, spikes to 500 QPS (short bursts).
2) Firewall: we can allow egress to Redwood IP range for Dedicated; will confirm CIDR next week.
3) Procurement turnaround: target sign by 2026-07-02 (we have an internal deadline).

Decision: we will run Hosted PoC in us-west with pseudonymized traffic for Weeks 1-2, run Dedicated scale test in Weeks 3-5, and hold final checkpoint Week 6 to decide production lane. We have also attached a populated MAP sheet with business acceptance criteria.

Please confirm you have the MAP with economics and we'll lock the first working session on Monday 5/31.

Best,
Helen Park
Sr. Eng Manager, Cardio.IO
